à l'aube ou au crépuscule, quand le ciel: at dawn or dusk, when the sky is overcast (clouds, rain, storm or fog)
Tu connais l'histoire du vieux brochet d: Do you know the story of the old pike of the lake? It has lived in the Mountain lake longer than I have. My father hooked it once: it snapped his rod in two. Go and catch some pike up there, they will tell you where it hunts.
Regarde ces brochets : ils ont des trace: Look at these pike: they have tooth marks on their backs. Those are its teeth. It hunts at dawn and dusk. Fish at the lake at those hours: if it swims past your line, it may lose a golden scale.
A golden scale! It really is alive. It only bites a golden frog: two feathers, four scales and its own scale so it can smell it. Make it at the workshop.
Monte au lac à l'aube ou au crépuscule,: Go up to the lake at dawn or dusk, when the sky is overcast, and cast far. It fights in three stages: it dives, it jumps, then it gives everything it has left. Don't pull when it jumps.
Tu l'as sorti ! Personne au village ne l: You landed it! Nobody in the village had ever seen it whole. I'll tell everyone, and your name with it.
la nuit, quand la lune est plus qu'à moi: at night, when the moon is more than half full
Les nuits de lune, je vois une lueur sou: On moonlit nights I see a glow under the water of the pond. The old folks call it the moon carp. Catch some carp here: they swim with it.
Tes carpes sentent la lune… Elle est pas: Your carp smell of the moon… It swam close by. At night it sometimes leaves a moon pearl behind. Fish at the pond after sunset.
Une perle de lune ! Mélange-la avec deux: A moon pearl! Mix it with two fireflies and three scales: a moon ball is the only thing it eats.
Reviens à l'étang la nuit, quand la lune: Come back to the pond at night, when the moon is more than half full: look at it in the sky. It dives, it jumps, then it struggles with all its strength.
Elle brille encore dans ta main… Je sava: It still glows in your hand… I knew it existed. Thank you for showing it to me.
Sur la banquise, j'ai vu une ombre plus: On the ice floe I saw a shadow bigger than my boat pass under the ice. The ice king. Bring me three rare fish from there: it only hunts the best.
Ces poissons ont des marques de givre. I: These fish have frost marks. It is prowling. Fish on the ice floe at night, when it snows: it sometimes breaks a tooth on the ice.
Une dent de glace, longue comme mon bras: An ice tooth, as long as my arm! With four ice crystals and three scales, make a frosted herring. It's its favourite meal.
Retourne sur la banquise la nuit, sous l: Go back to the ice floe at night, in the snow. Take a strong rod: it dives, it jumps, then it strikes from every side.
Le roi des glaces ! Je pourrai enfin dir: The ice king! At last I can tell the harbour I wasn't dreaming.
